newsitem.title: USA: U.S. House censures Mexico in rebuff to Clinton.
newsitem.headline: U.S. House censures Mexico in rebuff to Clinton.

text.p: The House of Representatives on Thursday voted to overturn President Bill Clinton's finding that Mexico is an ally in the war on drugs but agreed to give it 90 days to improve its performance.

The House approved a resolution -- which would need Senate backing and faces the threat of a presidential veto -- that would black-list Mexico but would waive the economic sanctions usually involved and would also give Mexico the 90-day grace period.

Faced with both White House opposition and bitter resentment from Mexico, the House first softened the blow by amending the resolution to give Clinton the 90 days to obtain "reliable assurances of substantial progress" by Mexico as a drug-war ally.

The basic resolution overturned Clinton's own finding of last month that Mexico had already proved itself in that regard. But it also suspended the sanctions usually required by so-called decertification, including a ban on U.S. aid and a requirement to oppose any loans to Mexico by international financial institutions.

Clinton had certified Mexico despite charges by congressional critics that its government was riddled with corruption that compromised its effectiveness in the drug war. Mexico has expressed indignation at the U.S. political debate over its integrity and promised unspecified retaliation if the black-listing resolution passed.
